vulnerable.evidence: Object prototype polluted via _.defaultsDeep constructor.prototype path

fixed.evidence: malicious defaultsDeep completed without observable prototype pollution

oracle.explanation: Uses lodash public API _.defaultsDeep, which is affected in vulnerable lodash versions by prototype pollution through constructor.prototype. The oracle first verifies a benign defaultsDeep merge works; only then sets operation_completed=true. It then applies a malicious payload and checks whether Object.prototype receives a unique marker. Pollution means exploit_succeeded=true (vulnerable behavior). If patched, no pollution occurs (and possibly an exception), yielding exploit_succeeded=false while keeping operation_completed=true.

attempts.explanation: This oracle tests lodash prototype pollution via the public _.merge API. It first performs a benign merge to confirm ordinary functionality; only after that succeeds does it mark operation_completed=true. It then supplies a malicious object containing __proto__ and checks whether a new empty object inherits the injected property. In vulnerable versions, Object.prototype is polluted and exploit_succeeded=true. In patched versions, pollution is prevented (or malicious merge throws), yielding exploit_succeeded=false while operation_completed remains true. Any setup/module/benign failure reports operation_completed=false.
attempts.validation_reason: Expected vulnerable=EXPLOIT_SUCCEEDED and fixed=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED; got vulnerable=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED and fixed=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED.

attempts.explanation: This oracle uses lodash's public _.set API, which is vulnerable in older releases (including 4.17.11) to prototype pollution when given a path containing __proto__. It first performs a benign _.set call to verify normal operation and only then marks operation_completed=true. Next it performs a malicious _.set({}, '__proto__.__oracle_pp_flag__', 'PWNED') and checks whether a fresh plain object inherits that marker. In vulnerable versions, the marker appears on Object.prototype (exploit_succeeded=true). In patched versions, the marker should not appear (exploit_succeeded=false). Any setup/module/benign failure reports operation_completed=false.
attempts.validation_reason: Expected vulnerable=EXPLOIT_SUCCEEDED and fixed=EXPLOIT_BLOCKED; got vulnerable=EXPLOIT_SUCCEEDED and fixed=EXPLOIT_SUCCEEDED.

attempts.explanation: This oracle targets lodash prototype pollution by exercising _.merge, which is a public API implicated in lodash 4.17.11 pollution issues. It first performs a benign merge and validates expected behavior; only then does it set operation_completed=true. The malicious step uses a constructor.prototype payload (not just __proto__) to distinguish patched behavior that may specifically block one vector. The oracle declares exploit success only if a fresh object inherits the injected marker from Object.prototype. If the malicious call throws after benign success, that is treated as blocked (exploit_succeeded=false) with evidence. Any setup/module/benign failure reports operation_completed=false as required.
